Section 1 — Accredited Hospitals & Health Facilities

CHUNK 1 — Overview of Accredited Facilities

As of 2024, over 3,400 healthcare facilities are accredited by NHIA across Ghana.

Any NHIA-accredited facility must accept your valid NHIS card for covered services.

Types of accredited facilities:

Teaching Hospitals (Tertiary Care) | Regional Hospitals | District Hospitals

Polyclinics | Health Centres | CHPS Compounds

Private Clinics and Hospitals | Maternity Homes

Pharmacies | Licensed Chemical Shops | Diagnostic Centres | Laboratories

How to confirm accreditation: visit www.nhis.gov.gh, call your nearest district office,

or call the NHIA helpline: 0544446447.

[category: hospitals]  [tags: accredited facilities, 3400, CHPS, pharmacy, private clinic, district]

1.1 Teaching Hospitals (Tertiary Care)

CHUNK 2 — Major Teaching Hospitals

These are the five NHIA-accredited Teaching Hospitals providing specialized tertiary care:

1. Korle Bu Teaching Hospital — Accra

2. Komfo Anokye Teaching Hospital — Kumasi

3. Tamale Teaching Hospital — Tamale

4. Cape Coast Teaching Hospital — Cape Coast

5. Ho Teaching Hospital — Ho

Teaching hospitals accept referrals from lower-level facilities.

NHIS covers services at teaching hospitals for covered conditions.

1.4 Free Dialysis Facilities (Since December 2024)

CHUNK 5 — Free Dialysis: 20 Designated Hospitals

Since December 2024, NHIS covers FREE dialysis for all registered kidney patients at these 20 hospitals:

1. Komfo Anokye Teaching Hospital    2. Cape Coast Teaching Hospital

3. Korle Bu Teaching Hospital          4. Ghana Police Hospital

5. Trust Hospital Premium Centre      6. Ridge Regional Hospital

7. International Maritime Hospital    8. Tamale Teaching Hospital

9. Bolgatanga Regional Hospital       10. Upper West Regional Hospital

11. Ho Teaching Hospital              12. Volta Regional Hospital — Hohoe

13. Effia Nkwanta Regional Hospital   14. Takoradi Hospital

Free dialysis requires registration as a kidney patient under NHIS.

Dialysis at non-designated facilities is not covered under NHIS.

Section 2 — NHIS Medicines List

CHUNK 6 — Key Facts: NHIS Medicines List (2025)

The 2025 NHIS Medicines List contains 551 approved medicines.

Medicines are listed by generic (International Non-Proprietary) names — NOT brand names.

The list is reviewed and updated annually in consultation with healthcare providers.

Only credentialed providers can prescribe medicines under NHIS.

Medicines must be prescribed using the exact names on the approved list.

If a pharmacy says they only have the branded version, ask for a generic equivalent first.

Personal abbreviations and brand-only names are NOT accepted on NHIS claims forms.

To verify if a medicine is on the list, call: 0544446447.

[category: medicines]  [tags: 551 medicines, generic, formulary, prescription, brand, 2025]

CHUNK 7 — Who Can Prescribe NHIS Medicines

The following healthcare workers are authorised to prescribe NHIS medicines:

— Medical Practitioners (Doctors)

— Dentists

— Midwives

— Medical Assistants

— Nurses in specialized fields

Only practitioners at NHIA-credentialed facilities can prescribe under NHIS.

[category: medicines]  [tags: prescribers, doctors, midwives, nurses, medical assistant, dentist]

CHUNK 8 — Common Medicine Categories Covered

Analgesics (Pain Relief): Paracetamol (most prescribed), Diclofenac, Aspirin

Antimalarials: Artemether-Lumefantrine (second most prescribed), Artesunate

Anti-infectives: Metronidazole, Amoxicillin, Ciprofloxacin, Azithromycin

Antihypertensives: Amlodipine, Atenolol, Bisoprolol, Ramipril

Diabetes Medications: Metformin, Glibenclamide, Tolbutamide, Insulin

Cardiovascular: Warfarin, Aspirin, Statins, Amiodarone

Respiratory: Salbutamol inhaler, Budesonide, Theophylline

Gastrointestinal: Omeprazole, Ranitidine, Metoclopramide

Mental Health: Chlorpromazine, Haloperidol, Risperidone, Amitriptyline

Antibiotics/Antimicrobials: Penicillin, Ceftriaxone, Clindamycin, Doxycycline

Oncology (selected): Anastrozole, Tamoxifen, Capecitabine, Carboplatin

[category: medicines]  [tags: analgesics, antimalarials, antibiotics, diabetes, cardiovascular, categories]

CHUNK 9 — Medicines NOT Included in NHIS List

The following are NOT reimbursable under the NHIS medicines list:

— Medical devices and supplies

— Anesthetic agents (included in procedure tariffs separately)

— Childhood immunizations (covered under separate immunization program)

— Tuberculosis medications (covered under TB control program)

— HIV/AIDS antiretroviral drugs (covered under National AIDS Control Program)

— Some mental health medications (covered under mental health program)

— Family planning services (covered under reproductive health program)

[category: medicines]  [tags: excluded medicines, immunization, TB, ARV, HIV, anaesthetic, family planning]

Section 3 — NHIS Benefits Package

CHUNK 10 — Benefits Overview

The NHIS benefit package covers approximately 95% of disease conditions affecting Ghanaians.

The scheme provides comprehensive coverage with:

— No co-payments or deductibles for covered services

— No annual or lifetime limits on coverage

— Financial protection against catastrophic healthcare costs

— Access regardless of ability to pay at point of service

— Portable across all districts in Ghana

[category: benefits]  [tags: 95%, no co-payment, no deductible, coverage, portable]

3.1 Outpatient Services

CHUNK 11 — Outpatient Services Covered

General consultations and examinations

Specialist consultations (all specialties)

Diagnostic testing and laboratory services

Minor operations and procedures

Hernia repair

Wound dressing

Physiotherapy services

Medicines from the NHIS Medicines List

Follow-up visits for chronic conditions (diabetes, hypertension, epilepsy, asthma, cardiovascular)

[category: benefits]  [tags: outpatient, consultation, specialist, laboratory, physiotherapy, chronic disease]

3.2 Inpatient Services

CHUNK 12 — Inpatient Services Covered

Hospital accommodation (general ward only — not VIP or private ward)

Medical and nursing care

Specialist inpatient care

Most surgical procedures

Post-operative care

Intensive Care Unit (ICU) services

Meals during hospitalization

Medications during admission (from NHIS medicines list)

[category: benefits]  [tags: inpatient, ward, surgery, ICU, post-operative, nursing, meals]

3.3 Maternity Care (100% Free)

CHUNK 13 — Maternity Care (Fully Covered)

ALL maternity care is 100% free for registered NHIS members:

— Ante-natal care (all visits and all tests)

— Normal delivery

— Caesarean section deliveries

— Post-natal care (up to 6 weeks after delivery)

— Neonatal care

Pregnant women are EXEMPT from NHIS premiums entirely.

Pregnant women are also exempt from the 3-month waiting period.

A facility that charges a registered member for maternity care is in violation of NHIS policy.

Report to: 0544446447 or info@nhia.gov.gh

[category: benefits]  [tags: maternity, antenatal, delivery, caesarean, postnatal, neonatal, free, 100%]

CHUNK 14 — Oral Health & Eye Care

Oral Health: Dental consultations, tooth extractions, dental treatments, oral procedures

Eye Care: Eye examinations, treatment for eye conditions, selected eye surgery

Note: Optical aids (glasses, contact lenses) and hearing aids are NOT covered under NHIS.

CHUNK 17 — Specialized Services (New 2024)

Since December 2024: Free dialysis for all registered kidney patients at 20 designated hospitals.

Breast cancer treatment — covered under NHIS.

Cervical cancer treatment — covered under NHIS.

Cancer screening services — covered under NHIS.

Most other cancer treatments are NOT covered under NHIS.

Organ transplants are NOT covered under NHIS.

Section 4 — Services NOT Covered (Exclusions)

CHUNK 18 — Medical Procedures Not Covered

The following medical procedures are excluded from the NHIS benefits package:

— Cosmetic surgery (unless medically necessary)

— Organ transplants

— Dialysis for chronic renal failure (EXCEPT at the 20 designated free dialysis centres)

— Most cancer treatments (EXCEPT breast and cervical cancer)

— Echocardiography

— Angiography

— Assisted reproduction services (IVF, surrogacy)

— Experimental or investigational treatments

— Overseas diagnosis and treatment

— VIP or private ward accommodation (only general ward covered)

[category: benefits, exclusions]  [tags: excluded, not covered, cosmetic, transplant, angiography, IVF, overseas]

CHUNK 19 — Medical Devices & Aids Not Covered

The following medical devices and aids are NOT covered under NHIS:

— Optical aids (glasses, contact lenses)

— Hearing aids

— Orthopedic aids (prosthetics, wheelchairs, crutches)

[category: benefits, exclusions]  [tags: glasses, hearing aid, prosthetics, wheelchair, optical, orthopedic]

Section 5 — Exempted Categories (No Premium Required)

CHUNK 20 — Complete List of Exempted Categories

The following categories pay NO premium. They may only pay a small registration/renewal processing fee:

1. Children — All persons below 18 years. Free if at least one parent/guardian is a valid NHIS member.

2. Pregnant Women — Free coverage for ante-natal, delivery, and post-natal care (up to 6 weeks).

3. Elderly (70+) — Persons above 70 years of age. May pay a small processing fee but no premium.

4. SSNIT Contributors — 2.5% deduction from SSNIT contributions serves as their premium.

5. SSNIT Pensioners — All pensioners of SSNIT.

6. Indigents — Persons classified as indigent by the Minister for Social Welfare.

7. Persons with Disabilities — Categories determined by the Minister for Social Welfare.

8. Mental Health Patients — Persons with diagnosed mental disorders.

9. LEAP Beneficiaries — Beneficiaries of the Livelihood Empowerment Against Poverty program.

Approximately 65% of active NHIS members fall under exempted categories.
